stem: A client with epilepsy who takes an antiseizure medication is planning pregnancy. Which teaching is most appropriate?

options.A: Stop the antiseizure medication independently before conception because all antiseizure medications have the same fetal-risk profile.
options.B: Arrange preconception review so seizure control and medication-specific fetal risks can be optimized, and discuss recommended folic acid supplementation with the clinician.
options.C: Continue the regimen without preconception discussion because pregnancy does not affect antiseizure-medication treatment decisions.
options.D: Avoid folic acid because supplementation is contraindicated for people who take antiseizure medications.

rationale: The 2024 AAN/AES/SMFM guideline recommends optimizing antiseizure medication choice and dose for both seizure control and fetal outcomes at the earliest possible opportunity before conception. It also recommends at least 0.4 mg of folic acid daily before conception and during pregnancy for people with epilepsy who take an antiseizure medication. B is therefore the best teaching. A falsely treats all medications as equivalent and encourages unsupervised treatment change, C omits recommended preconception optimization, and D contradicts the guideline's folic-acid recommendation.
educational_objective: Teach clients with epilepsy who are planning pregnancy to seek preconception antiseizure-medication review and to discuss guideline-recommended folic acid supplementation rather than changing therapy independently.
source_organization: American Academy of Neurology (AAN), American Epilepsy Society (AES), and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM)
source_document_title: Teratogenesis, Perinatal, and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes After In Utero Exposure to Antiseizure Medication: Practice Guideline From the AAN, AES, and SMFM
source_version_date: Practice Guideline May 2024; Neurology publication June 2024; current AAN guideline page rechecked 2026-08-16
source_locator: Major recommendations in abstract/clinician guidance — optimize ASM and dose preconceptionally; prescribe at least 0.4 mg folic acid daily preconceptionally and during pregnancy
source_claim_supported: For people with epilepsy of childbearing potential, antiseizure therapy should be optimized for seizure control and fetal outcomes as early as possible before conception, and folic acid supplementation of at least 0.4 mg/day is recommended before and during pregnancy.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed p.12, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — educate client about medications and review pertinent medication-related data; integrated reproductive-health teaching
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — antiseizure medication planning before pregnancy

source_original.stem: A client taking an antiseizure medication plans pregnancy. Which teaching is most appropriate?

options.A: Stop all antiseizure medication immediately because every agent carries the same fetal risk
options.B: Arrange preconception review because fetal risks vary by drug, and do not stop therapy abruptly
options.C: Continue the current regimen without discussion because pregnancy does not affect treatment choices
options.D: Avoid folic acid because supplementation is contraindicated with antiseizure medication therapy

source_original.rationale: Current AAN/AES/SMFM guidance emphasizes optimizing antiseizure therapy before pregnancy when possible, balancing seizure control with medication-specific fetal risks, and using folic acid. Abrupt discontinuation can endanger the patient and fetus.
source_original.source_detail: Practice Guideline, May 2024: teratogenesis, perinatal and neurodevelopmental outcomes; folic acid and medication selection; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Removed the broad unsupported abrupt-discontinuation claim from the rationale and keyed option, anchored teaching directly to the 2024 AAN/AES/SMFM preconception and folic-acid recommendations, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: AAN/AES/SMFM 2024 practice guideline; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: AAN page identifies the May 2024 guideline as replacing the 2009 pregnancy parameter; rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The current guideline directly supports earliest-possible preconception medication optimization and at least 0.4 mg/day folic acid before and during pregnancy.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect; medication fetal risks are not uniform and independent treatment cessation is not the recommended preconception strategy.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; preconception medication optimization is specifically recommended.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; folic acid is recommended, not contraindicated.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B combines the two central guideline-supported preconception actions.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are pregnancy medication-teaching strategies; key selection requires guideline knowledge.
audit_findings.blueprint: NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read AAN current guideline page and PubMed recommendations, removed the unsupported abrupt-stop rationale language, challenged all choices for overstatement, and confirmed B remained uniquely correct.
